Injection 7 fully resolved every pair with useful resolution margin, but its last peak eluted during the final hold. Keep its starting composition and temperature while raising phi1 to bring the last peak into the gradient and target elution within 10 minutes.

Reduce gradient steepness modestly to lift the sole critical pair from R = 1.20 toward baseline resolution. Keeping the composition window and temperature fixed isolates the slope effect, with the last peak expected near 10 minutes.
Injection 10 already achieves the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Raise temperature one step to seek a shorter fully resolved run while testing whether the critical pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Test higher temperature beyond the apparent critical-pair crossover at 45 C, where selectivity may recover with reversed elution order. Lower phi0 to protect the early pair from temperature-driven compression, retaining injection 10 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Shorten injection 12’s gradient by one grid step to seek a faster method at the maximum CRF. Keeping composition and temperature fixed tests whether both critical pairs remain at R ≥ 1.5 under modestly increased steepness.

Lower the starting organic fraction to test whether shifting the elution window restores resolution of injection 13’s sole critical pair. Retain the 10-minute gradient to seek a fully resolved run faster than injection 12, which remains the fastest maximum-score method.

Increase gradient steepness by one endpoint step to shorten injection 14 while seeking to preserve full resolution. The slope comparison at 55 C suggests the closest pair may tolerate this change, while the other critical pair has modest resolution margin.

Test one temperature step higher to shorten the fastest fully resolved method without further steepening its gradient. Monitor both marginal pairs for selectivity changes, retaining injection 15 if either falls below R = 1.5.

Return to 55 C to avoid the co-elution seen at 60 C. Lower phi0 to improve the slope-sensitive pair while raising phi1 to seek faster final elution, checking whether the other close pair retains baseline resolution.

Raise phi1 one step to test the speed limit around injection 17, the fastest fully resolved method so far. Both critical pairs have little margin, so retain injection 17 if this steeper gradient drops either below R = 1.5.

The 55 C branch has reached a resolution limit, so explore lower-temperature selectivity with a steep gradient and a low starting organic fraction. This tests a different route to faster full separation while retaining injection 17 as the fastest maximum-score method.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 60 C moves the co-eluting pair seen in injection 16 beyond its selectivity crossover into resolved, reversed elution order. This explores a substantially faster method while retaining injection 17 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score option.

Further steepen the gradient to test whether the apparently reversed critical pair gains enough separation to reach R ≥ 1.5. Keep phi0 fixed to protect early retention while monitoring the neighboring pair for compression.

Return to the successful 40 C selectivity region, lowering phi0 relative to injection 9 to test whether it offsets resolution loss from a steeper gradient. This explores another route to faster full separation while preserving injection 17 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Trim injection 17’s unused gradient tail while preserving its slope and temperature: its last peak eluted at approximately phi = 0.57. This should retain full resolution and the maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient, although final retention time should remain essentially unchanged.

Test a fine increase in slope from injection 15’s 0.065 to 0.0667 organic fraction per minute, targeting slightly earlier final elution. This probes the full-resolution boundary without the larger slope jump that failed in injection 18.

Use the final injection to test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the reversed critical pair from injection 20 without the severe compression seen in injection 21. Retain injection 17 or 23 as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method if this faster candidate loses resolution.
